mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprises in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically different from the prior month's returns (p > 0.10), or the 5-day return is positive despite the rate spike.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress equity real returns, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day rolling average of 60-day returns is positive across 4 consecutive months after the trigger, or inflation surprise decays rapidly (<1% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and a decline in UNRATE over the same month indicates strengthening labor market conditions without wage suppression, which tends to boost equity risk premia and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening without wage inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >70% of similar labor market events, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE and SPX returns falls below 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (real private consumption) above the prior quarter's average, accompanied by a positive HOUST reading, suggests robust demand momentum that supports higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > QoQ average and HOUST > prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in 3 out of 4 similar monthly surges, or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for lagged SPX and macro variables.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% signals supply-side softness that raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Three consecutive months of INDPRO < previous month and decline ≥ 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative even after excluding supply shocks, or INDPRO recovers rapidly (<2% decline over 2 months).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below 3.5% for three consecutive months during a non-recessionary regime, it supports accommodative monetary policy that lowers real rates and tends to drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.5% for three consecutive months and not in recession period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in 80% of similar low-rate episodes, or the effect disappears after controlling for yield curve slope and yield spreads.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE accompanied by a sustained rise in PAYEMS (>3 months) suggests wage growth is decoupling from labor supply, which can indicate inflationary pressures and tends to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls >0.5pp for 3 consecutive months while PAYEMS rises
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >60% of analogous episodes, or wage–labor supply dynamics revert to neutrality.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in RSAFS (retail sales) above the prior 6 months' average, occurring when CPIAUCSL is flat, signals resilient consumer demand that supports equity risk appetite and positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-month average and CPIAUCSL flat in the same month
regime_hint: Resilient demand in a neutral inflation environment
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >50% of similar spikes, or the effect is not robust after rolling regression controls.
